svg.title: P22 simultaneous finite-sample certification of physical-refinement chains
svg.desc: Publication-style theorem map showing one base confidence event, deterministic pushforward control, simultaneous residual intervals, and simultaneous refinement-gain intervals.
svg.text: P22 · Simultaneous Finite-Sample Certification of Refinement Chains
One confidence event for the base physical-target law controls the entire declared descriptor chain.
ONE BASE EVENT
Certify the empirical base law once
‖PΩE − P̂ΩE‖TV ≤ τn(α)
Pr(event) ≥ 1 − α
The radius depends on the base alphabet dΩ dE, not on the number of descriptor levels.
RESIDUAL PUSHFORWARDS
All P21 residual levels share the event
φk(ω,e) = (ω,Tk(ω),e)
|Rk − R̂k| ≤ Δk(τn)
The inequalities hold simultaneously for k = 0,…,m.
A positive terminal lower bound certifies persistence at the finest tested level.
GAIN PUSHFORWARDS
All refinement gains share the same event
ψk(ω,e) = (Tk(ω),Tk−1(ω),e)
|Gk − Ĝk| ≤ Γk(τn)
P21 also gives Gk = Rk−1 − Rk at population and empirical levels.
Intersecting direct and difference intervals can tighten the certificate.
SIMULTANEOUS P22 GUARANTEE
The whole residual-and-gain trajectory is covered together
Pr( Rk ∈ IkR ∀k and Gk ∈ IkG ∀k ) ≥ 1 − α
No replacement of α by α/(2m+1) is needed because one base-TV event implies every level-specific bound.
Long chains are not free: large alphabets can make the shared finite-sample radius numerically weak.
INTERPRETATION BOUNDARY
Certified terminal persistence challenges the finest declared descriptor under the model; it does not prove physical completeness or nonphysical ontology.
The identity-descriptor boundary I(E;Ω | Ω)=0 remains unchanged.
